## How they got there
Manchester City won the tournament by beating Inter 1-0 in the final after progressing through a knockout phase containing 16 teams. Their profile was defined by dominating attacks per game at 69.2, where they were better than 100% of that season's group/league-phase teams, alongside an exceptional goal difference per game of 2.0 which placed them ahead of 94% of peers. They also excelled in discipline with fouls committed per game at 8.2, a figure better than 92% of the same cohort.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model assigned Manchester City a 27.1% probability of reaching the final, which is significantly higher than the base rate of 12.5%, yet they ranked only third among all knockout teams by that metric. Because ranks three and four make a team a leading contender while any lower rank means the model did not pick them, this third-place ranking indicates the model viewed them as a top two candidate rather than an automatic selection. Consequently, the stage nearest to the model's expectation of 1.82 was the semi-finals, suggesting the algorithm would have predicted a slightly earlier exit than their actual victory.

## Weak spots
The team's statistical profile shows clear vulnerabilities in long passes (% of passes) at 9.1, where they were better than only 12% of that season's group/league-phase teams, and distance covered per game (km) at 116.2, beating just 66%. Although the model marked down opponent shots per game (lower is better) with a negative SHAP contribution of -0.07, Manchester City actually ranked highly on this stat by being better than 94% of that season's group/league-phase teams.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
